attacks.claim: Retrieval moves to Nimbus Vector Store, provisioned only in us-east-2 with EU regions on a roadmap. Week 2 re-embeds ~41M chunks of customer documents there and dual-writes new documents. This breaches the agreed DPA constraint that documents and derived data (chunks, embeddings, prompts) be processed and stored in the EU, and no transfer mechanism is stated.
attacks.evidence: "Vector Store is in public preview and currently provisioned in us-east-2, with EU regions on Nimbus's GA roadmap." / "Week 2: re-embed corpus (~41M chunks) into Nimbus Vector Store; dual-write new documents."

attacks.claim: The 4,100-case regression suite is the agreed release gate for any model change, but the plan moves it to week 6+, after the week 4 all-tenant cutover. Production would receive an unvalidated model and prompt set. The 25-question blind comparison cannot substitute for the gate.
attacks.evidence: "the full regression suite run moves to post-migration hardening (week 6+) rather than blocking cutover."

attacks.claim: Week 3 irreversibly deletes fine-tuned checkpoints and LoRA adapters and releases the A100 reservation, and week 5 removes pgvector, the vLLM manifests and the GPU pool. All of this happens before cutover validation and the regression gate, so there is no rollback path if quality or compliance fails.
attacks.evidence: "Week 3: release the A100 reservation ... and delete fine-tuned checkpoints and LoRA adapters from object storage" / "Week 5: remove pgvector, vLLM manifests, and GPU node pool from Terraform."

attacks.claim: The quality-parity claim rests on 25 support-inbox questions rated by two lawyers (19 preferred). That is far too small, and it does not cover practice-area behaviour (LoRA replaced by unprototyped system prompts), long-context cases, or retrieval quality after switching to embed-3 and re-embedding the whole corpus.
attacks.evidence: "ran 25 representative questions from the support inbox through both stacks ... This confirms quality parity or better"

attacks.claim: Zero data retention is cited for the org account, but the plan does not state that it covers embed-3 or Vector Store (a preview product), or that the DPA sub-processor terms cover them. Retention of customer content and embeddings at Nimbus is unverified.
attacks.evidence: "Zero data retention is enabled on our org account (signed addendum, ref NMB-ZDR-2291)." ABSENT: retention/sub-processor coverage for embed-3 and Vector Store

attacks.claim: A public-preview Vector Store with no stated SLA becomes the sole retrieval path, and after week 5 there is no alternate inference or retrieval path. The plan has no fallback, degraded mode, or exit plan for a Nimbus outage or deprecation.
attacks.evidence: "Vector Store is in public preview" / "remove pgvector, vLLM manifests, and GPU node pool from Terraform"

attacks.claim: Tenant isolation relies on per-tenant collections and keys on a preview managed service. The plan specifies no cross-tenant leakage test or verification. Failure would expose one law firm's documents to another.
attacks.evidence: "Tenant isolation in Vector Store uses one collection per tenant with a tenant-scoped API key, mirroring today's per-tenant pgvector schemas."

attacks.claim: Latency was measured from Frankfurt over one window, while the target is Dublin generation plus us-east-2 retrieval. It covers only TTFT at normal load, not the long-context workloads that motivate the move. The rate-limit math ignores the week 2 re-embedding load sharing the contracted tier.
attacks.evidence: "Atlas-L p95 time-to-first-token measured at 640 ms from our Frankfurt pods (1,000 requests, week of 10-05)" / "our contracted tier allows 120 req/s"

attacks.claim: The cost estimates have no stated basis (token volume, per-token price, vector footprint). The one-time re-embed of 41M chunks and the dual-run period are excluded. Enabling 200k context has no spend cap. Early release of the A100 reservation is assumed penalty-free and happens before cutover.
attacks.evidence: "Nimbus generation (est.) | $0 | $7,900" / "release the A100 reservation (saves $18.4k/mo from the next billing cycle)"
